AUTHOR: Martija
TITLE: SynDHN: Multi-Object Fish Tracker Trained on Synthetic Underwater Videos
DATA: Own/partner field videos from several Philippine benthic sites (Labao & Naval; UP MSI); synthetic MOT dataset (6 sites) for training; real test set 4 videos from other sites
V_EV: Table III (test set statistics) site descriptions: 'water column, heavy marine snow'; Sec III-A: 'Each site has different water, illumination, hue, and background conditions'
D2: train synthetic 3000 frames (6 sites) + val; real test 450 frames from 4 videos at different sites
D_EV: Sec IV-C: 'We take 4 underwater videos taken from sites that are different from the sites we used in generating our synthetic dataset.'
R_EV: Sec IV-C: test videos are from the same Philippine video collection, 'taken from sites that are different from the sites we used' (same campaign, P2)
C_EV: Table IV/V report identity switches (IDs); Sec IV-E: 'IDF1 score increases by 1.6 points and the number of identity switches is almost halved.'
E_EV: Sec IV-D: 'we only focus our evaluation on the most important ones, namely the IDF1 Score [46], the Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA)'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN (ResNet-50 FPN) + modified Deep Hungarian Network (spatial + appearance cues); PANet for blob extraction
NOTE: Detector pre-trained on prior Labao & Naval fish detection dataset (Philippine videos); DHN trained on synthetic videos built from field footage of 6 sites; real test on 4 videos from different sites in same collection -> R1=N per P2 (synthetic-to-real shift not counted as external, verify). Platform/camera not described (PLAT=NR). C: only association-threshold sensitivity (Fig 6), no detection score threshold value -> C1=NR; ID switches measured counted as C5 (verify). NIMG = real test frames.
